papers.title: Improved Training of Strong Stochastic Flow Maps
papers.abstract: Stochastic flow maps promise few-step sampling of stochastic differential equations (SDEs) by learning to directly jump between times along the solution path, yet training these models to learn this solution map remains difficult. The primary obstacle is the Brownian path itself: it is an infinite-dimensional object which needs to be passed to the neural network and is nowhere differentiable, which makes the implementation of derivative-based losses that power the state-of-the-art deterministic flow maps just out of reach. We identify two core design principles which address these issues: a) represent the Brownian path with a basis which carries higher-order local information, and b) train with an objective that forces the network to use the full representation of the path, not just the first order. To address this, we leverage the shifted Legendre polynomial expansion with a Wong-Zakai styled objective, unlocking derivative-based losses. Finally, we propose a recipe for fine-tuning large pre-trained flow models into strong stochastic flow maps. We ablate through this design space on several toy problems and use our findings to transform a large flow model into a strong stochastic flow map on ImageNet, achieving roughly a three-fold improvement in FD-DINOv2 over SSFM at four NFE.

papers.title: Rigorous integration of semilinear parabolic PDEs: forward evolution bounds and projected boundary value problems
papers.abstract: In this work, we present a rigorous integrator for initial and boundary value problems for semilinear parabolic PDEs. The method builds on earlier semigroup-based approaches while improving the bounds used in the fixed-point argument and extending the class of problems that can be treated. In particular, it controls the solution operator without requiring backward integration of the variational equation and allows projected boundary value problems to be studied through a simplified construction of an approximate inverse for the linearized operator. To illustrate the scope of the method, we present three applications to the two-dimensional Ohta--Kawasaki equation. For two initial value problems, we prove global existence and obtain explicit enclosures valid for all sufficiently large times around numerical approximations of stripe and spot equilibria. These results use a fixed-point formulation on an unbounded time interval, avoiding the construction of trapping regions. We also rigorously solve a projected boundary value problem with endpoint conditions chosen from linear approximations of the unstable and stable spaces of two saddle equilibria. This provides a step toward the rigorous study of heteroclinic saddle-to-saddle connections.

papers.title: Neural Vector Field Transformations: Learning the Flow of Autonomous Systems by Conjugation to Explicitly Integrable Reference Flows
papers.abstract: We represent the flow map of an autonomous ODE $\dot x=f(x)$ as a conjugate $\Phi_t=F_\theta^{-1}\circ\Psi_t\circ F_\theta$ of an explicitly integrable reference flow $\Psi_t$ by an invertible neural network $F_\theta$, the neural vector field transformation. The representation is an exact flow for every parameter value and inherits the phase portrait of the reference. A $C^1$ conjugacy preserves the eigenvalues of equilibria, the periods and Floquet multipliers of periodic orbits and the frequency-amplitude relation of centers, so these invariants must be learnable parameters of $\Psi$. We give parametrized reference flows with explicit integral curves, show that an action-angle reference is Hamiltonian only if its learnable frequency map is a gradient, and show that an orientation-preserving $F_\theta$ cannot reverse the rotation sense of the reference, so it must be fixed before training. The main contribution is a training recipe: a push-forward equation residual made relative to $|f|$ and sampled log-uniformly in $|x|$ around an equilibrium, with the anchors $F_\theta(0)=0$, $DF_\theta(0)=I$; a symplectic transformation with the gradient-form frequency map; and invariants initialized from the field or data. With it the full spectrum of a three- and a six-dimensional nonlinear sink is recovered (eigenvalue deviation $8.3\times10^{-3}$ and relative error 2.3%, three seeds each), and the action-angle variables of a four-dimensional integrable Hamiltonian system with frequency maps and actions correct to a median of 0.09% and 0.22%, and an exactly symplectic flow. On a dispersive system a time-input network is eight times more accurate inside its horizon, and the data-only identification of the Van der Pol oscillator yields a conjugacy on the data region with the Floquet exponent 17% off; an oracle run with the true invariants frozen attributes this to the expressivity of $F_\theta$.

papers.title: On the gradient conjecture at infinity: Finite spherical length for gradient trajectories of definable potentials
papers.abstract: We prove that for every open $ U \subseteq \mathbb R^n $ the spherical projection of every gradient trajectory $\theta(t)$, $t \geq 0$, of a definable $C^1$-potential $F \colon U \to \mathbb R$ has finite length and, in particular, converges (directional convergence). In other words, every gradient trajectory of a definable $C^1$-potential has finite total angular motion. Here, definable means definable in an arbitrary o-minimal structure expanding the real field. Notably, the gradient trajectory in this result is an arbitrary solution of the gradient flow differential equation (whose solutions may not be unique) with no further assumptions: The gradient trajectory may be unbounded and diverge to infinity or it may be convergent. The established theorem therefore provides affirmative answers to both the gradient conjecture at infinity for definable potentials and the definable Thom gradient conjecture. We apply our theorem to the training of deep neural networks (DNNs) to conclude that, in the case of definable and continuously differentiable activation and loss functions, the spherical projection of the DNN training flow must always converge (directional convergence).

papers.title: Families of relative periodic orbits in the planar three-body problem via consecutive alignments
papers.abstract: Relative periodic orbits (RPOs) are solutions of the three-body problem that are periodic in a uniformly rotating reference frame and, in general, quasi-periodic in inertial coordinates. We present a numerical procedure for computing and continuing one-parameter families of RPOs of the planar Newtonian three-body problem. The method exploits consecutive syzygies, understood here as configurations in which the three bodies are aligned and their velocities satisfy the corresponding symmetry conditions. Matching the positions and momenta at two consecutive alignments reduces the computation of RPOs to a low-dimensional nonlinear problem. Its solutions are then numerically continued, and linear stability is determined from the nontrivial eigenvalues of the rotated monodromy matrix after removing the neutral directions associated with conserved quantities and continuous symmetries. The procedure is applied to several mass distributions and initial configurations, producing families of Poincar\'e, Hill, and binary-type solutions. These families exhibit transitions from nearly circular to highly eccentric motion, changes of stability near resonances and turning points, and absolute periodic solutions when the rotation angle is a rational multiple of 2{\pi}. In the Hill families, the continuation connects satellite configurations with circumstellar motion as the smallest body loses its gravitational binding to the intermediate body. Circumbinary and circumstellar configurations are also obtained in the binary regime. The results illustrate the dynamical diversity of RPOs and provide coherent three-body motions that can be used as prescribed trajectories in restricted four-body models.

papers.title: DeGroot Dynamics on Multiplex Networks with Directed and Acyclic Interlayer Connectivities
papers.abstract: In models of opinion dynamics, researchers typically examine how an individual's opinion on one topic is influenced by the opinions of their neighbors in a network. However, people's opinions on a topic are also influenced by their opinions and their neighbors' opinions on related topics. In an election, for example, the opinions of a voter on a variety of issues inform their opinions of electoral candidates. To consider the influence between people's opinions on multiple distinct topics, we study a multiplex extension of the traditional DeGroot consensus model. In our multiplex DeGroot model, different network layers represent distinct topics and directed interlayer edges (which are not allowed to form cycles) encode relationships between distinct topics. In our model, an individual's opinion on one topic is influenced both by the opinions of their neighbors on that topic and by their own opinions on related topics. We prove under mild conditions that our multiplex DeGroot model converges to a limit state. We also prove that strong connectedness in ``source layers'' (which represent fundamental beliefs) eventually yields a consensus opinion in each layer. In particular, we show that consensus on source layers can lead to consensus on other layers even when those layers otherwise would be polarized. By numerically simulating our multiplex DeGroot model on a two-layer network, we examine the effects on opinion dynamics of (1) different network structures and (2) different types of initial opinion data.

papers.title: Effective stability and sharp logarithmic time scales for Hamiltonian PDEs on the circle
papers.abstract: We prove effective stability and matching logarithmic upper bounds for small solutions of Hamiltonian PDEs on the one-dimensional torus. An analytic coefficient-majorant calculus and an explicit normal-form iteration yield stability times with logarithms of order $L^{1+1/p}/(\log L)^{1/p}$ for Gevrey weights and $L^{1+(q-1)/(pq+1)}$ for logarithmic ultra-differentiable weights, where $L=\log(1/\varepsilon)$ and $p\geq1$ measures the order dependence of the small divisors. Even frequencies are organized into the exact blocks $\{n,-n\}$; elementary frequency gaps and constant weights on these blocks close the energy estimate. We verify the hypotheses for convolution NLS, fractional NLS with every fixed noninteger exponent $\eta>1/2$, and a beam equation with a metric parameter and a variational gradient nonlinearity. Two fixed analytic nonlocal Hamiltonian PDEs admit finite-support solutions whose first prescribed norm amplification occurs on the same logarithmic scales along sequences $\varepsilon_n\to0$. The common lower theorem applies to every sufficiently small datum of each admissible equation. Its combination with these examples establishes sharpness of both regularity-dependent scales under the same analytic and arithmetic hypotheses.

papers.title: Ergodicity for stochastic neural field equations
papers.abstract: We investigate the well-posedness and long-time behavior of a general continuum neural field model with Gaussian noise on possibly unbounded domains. In particular, we give conditions for the existence of invariant probability measures by restricting the solution flow to an invariant subspace with a nonlocal metric. Under the assumption of a sufficiently large decay parameter relative to the noise intensity, the norm of the connectivity kernel operator, and the Lipschitz regularity of the activation function, we establish exponential ergodicity and exponential mixing of the associated Markovian Feller semigroup and the uniqueness of the invariant measure.

papers.title: Low-Dimensional Reduction of Mean-Field Coupled Dynamical Systems with Units Described by Two Real Variables: Classification and Applications
papers.abstract: Low-dimensional reduction is crucial for understanding network systems with many units. In a recent advance, Martens and Dharmavaram developed a theory of exact low-dimensional reduction for a general class of mean-field coupled dynamical systems characterized by a mean-field Lie-Scheffers structure. In this paper, we classify mean-field coupled dynamical systems with a mean-field Lie-Scheffers structure, where each unit is described by two real variables. Our classification is based on Gonz\'alez-L\'opez, Kamran, and Olver's local classification of Lie systems on the plane near generic points and yields 28 types of mean-field coupled dynamical systems. For mean-field coupled systems with units described by two real variables, we first present a general theory on classification and low-dimensional reduction based on the mean-field Lie-Scheffers structure, and then discuss applications to populations of coupled oscillators. We show that low-dimensional reduction is possible for a broad class of populations of limit-cycle oscillators, extending the previously reported reducible class of populations of Stuart-Landau oscillators to include many new models.

papers.title: Embeddings of Relative Dimension Groups for Zero-Dimensional Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: Let $\pi:(X,T)\rightarrow(Y,S)$ be a factor map between zero-dimensional dynamical systems, and let $X_0$ and $Y_0$ be quasi-sections with $\pi(X_0)=Y_0$. We study the homomorphism $\pi^*:K^0(Y|Y_0,S)\rightarrow K^0(X|X_0,T)$, $[f]\mapsto[f\circ\pi]$, between the corresponding relative dimension groups, and identify it with the homomorphism induced by the premorphism between Bratteli--Vershik realizations associated with $\pi$. Generalizing a result of Glasner and Weiss for minimal Cantor systems, we show that if $Y_0$ is quasi-simple, then $\pi^*$ is an injective unital order-preserving homomorphism, and that if $X_0=\pi^{-1}(Y_0)$, then $\pi^*$ is a unital order embedding; the latter condition is characterized in terms of the premorphism. Examples show that quasi-simplicity cannot be dropped, and that without the condition $X_0=\pi^{-1}(Y_0)$ the map $\pi^*$ need not be an order embedding.

papers.title: Same Gaps, Different Sets: A Survey on Complimentary sets and their Dimensions
papers.abstract: Let a=\{a_n\} be a non-increasing sequence of positive real numbers adding up to $1$. Cutting out of the unit interval disjoint open gaps of lengths $a_1,a_2,\dots$, one for each term, leaves a compact set of Lebesgue measure zero, and since the gaps can be placed in infinitely many ways, there are infinitely many such sets. We call them the \emph{complementary sets} of $a$ and write $\mathfrak{C}_a$ for the family of all of them. Every set in $\mathfrak{C}_a$ is compact and totally disconnected, and all of them share the same gap lengths; what distinguishes one from another is only the arrangement of the gaps. Among them, the perfect sets are exactly the Cantor sets with those gaps, and they form a distinguished subclass. The central question of this survey is what such a rearrangement can change and what it cannot. The answer depends sharply on the notion of size: the box dimensions are constant on $\mathfrak{C}_a$, while the Hausdorff dimension attains every value in a closed interval whose endpoints are realised by two distinguished members, the Cantor set $C_a$ built by placing the gaps in a Cantor-like pattern, and the countable decreasing rearrangement $D_a$. We survey how this dichotomy persists, and how the roles of $C_a$ and $D_a$ are exchanged, across the intermediate dimensions of Falconer, Fraser and Kempton, the Assouad-type and $\Phi$-dimensions, and the Hausdorff and packing $h$-measures associated with a general dimension function; we also describe the almost sure behaviour of a randomly rearranged complementary set, where a sharp threshold in the depth of the scales examined separates two incompatible regimes. A final part restricts attention to the Cantor subclass and turns to the dynamical description of the sets C_a.

papers.title: Bistable Dynamics and Complete Classifications of A Seasonal Competition Model Between Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus
papers.abstract: The bistable dynamics and a complete classification of global dynamics are established for a competition model between Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus subject to favorable-unfavorable seasonal shifts, originally proposed by Zheng et al. (2025). More precisely, by employing Floquet theory, we prove that the unique positive periodic solution must be unstable. Consequently, bistable dynamics naturally emerge, which provides a rigorous theoretical validation of the numerical simulation results reported in the aforementioned work. Building on this, we further derive a full classification of the model's global dynamics. In addition, we carry out a comprehensive analysis of how seasonal switching mechanisms govern the competitive outcomes between these two mosquito species, thereby offering insights into their ecological coexistence and potential displacement.

papers.title: Frequency Structure of AMM Liquidity Pools: A Multiresolution Analysis of Regime Transitions
papers.abstract: This study examines the temporal structure of liquidity pools in constant-product automated market makers. Using a sample of eighteen pools observed at a five-minute frequency over two years, it aims to identify the temporal scales at which interactions within the system occur and how these interactions reorganize in response to changes in the volatility regime. Methodologically, the study proposes a strictly causal Haar multiresolution analysis in which each variable is estimated using only the information available at the time of measurement. Within this decomposition, three dimensions are examined: the scale composition of the return-to-risk relationship, the frequency-band coupling between pool activity and price volatility, and the detection of regime transitions using a fluctuation-to-trend indicator. The results reveal a clear structural segmentation: pool variability is concentrated at fast scales, whereas the relationships among its series, signal persistence, and information on subsequent performance reside at slow scales. Aggregate measures do not distinguish this separation because they combine both components before they can be compared.

papers.title: The minimal period solution of Hamiltonian systems with even potentials
papers.abstract: We consider the autonomous system $\ddot{q}+\nabla V(q)=0$ in an arbitrary finite-dimensional Euclidean space. The potential is assumed to be even, nonnegative and of class $C^2$, to satisfy $V(x)=o(|x|^2)$ at the origin, and the Ambrosetti--Rabinowitz superquadratic inequality outside a ball. We prove that, for every prescribed $T>0$, the system has a nonconstant solution with $T$ being its minimal positive period.

papers.title: Finite-to-One Maps into Band-Limited Function Spaces and Cubical Shifts with a Hurewicz Bound
papers.abstract: Let $(X,T)$ be a dynamical system with the marker property and finite mean dimension $m$. We prove that, for every integer $D>m$, there exists an equivariant continuous map $f:X\to([0,1]^D)^{\mathbb Z}$ whose fibers contain at most $\lfloor D/(D-m)\rfloor$ points; in particular, $f$ is an embedding when $D>2m$. This is the dynamical analogue of the fiber bound in Hurewicz's classical theorem (1933) for continuous maps into Euclidean cubes. For every real number $a>m$, we also construct an equivariant continuous map from $X$ into the closed unit ball of the real Bernstein space of bounded continuous functions on $\mathbb R$ whose Fourier transforms, understood in the sense of distributions, are supported in $[-a/2,a/2]$, with each fiber containing at most $\lfloor a/(a-m)\rfloor$ points. The proof adapts the signal-analysis method of Gutman--Qiao--Tsukamoto (2019) to the finite-to-one setting and simplifies its analytic and geometric ingredients for $\mathbb Z$-actions.

papers.title: Continuity of Furstenberg entropy on Bowen Poisson bundles
papers.abstract: We provide a sufficient criterion for continuity of the Furstenberg entropy of Bowen Poisson bundles, jointly in the random walk measure and the underlying invariant random subgroup. The criterion applies in particular for tree-like Poisson bundles of a free group and for intersectional invariant random subgroups on lamplighter groups. It also provides continuity of the boundary entropy spectrum of powers of prime measured groups.

papers.title: Linear Stability of Double-Double Orbits in the Equal-Mass Four-Body Problem via Index Theory
papers.abstract: In this paper, using the Maslov-type index theory in symplectic geometry, we study the linear stability of the double-double orbits in the planar equal-mass four body problem. By analyzing its symmetry properties and variational characterization, we clarify the relationship between linear stability and its variational nature on various loop spaces and show that for any rotation angle $\theta=\frac{\pi}{n}$, the retrograde double-double orbits are linearly stable with integer $n\in[3,30]$ and the prograde double-double orbits are linearly stable with integer $n\in[4,30]$. We also give the distributions of the eigenvalues on the unit circle of the monodromy matrices associated with the orbits. The basic idea is as follows: the variational characterization of the orbits provides information about its Morse index; based on its relation to the Maslov-type index, our stability criteria come into play.

papers.title: Solutions of $x^\alpha+y^\alpha=1$ in $\lambda$-Cantor sets
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the structure of the solutions of $x^\alpha+y^\alpha=1$ with both coordinates in a $\lambda$-Cantor set. We prove that, for any $\alpha>1$, the intersection with the middle-third Cantor set has positive Hausdorff dimension, strengthening the infinitude question posed by Jiang et al. [J. London Math. Soc. 113 (2026), e70408]. To explore the structure of the solutions, for arbitrary $\alpha$, we find that their Hausdorff dimension undergoes phase transitions as $\lambda$ varies: we establish the occurrence of Hausdorff phase transitions by proving the existence of zero-dimensional and positive-dimensional regions.

papers.title: Strong Positive Recurrence for Strongly Entropy Expanding Maps
papers.abstract: We introduce expanding strong positive recurrence (expanding-SPR) for non-invertible systems with critical points. We then give a sufficient condition for maps to be SPR: strong entropy expansion (SEE). We prove that expanding-SPR implies good thermodynamical properties, including exponential decay of correlations of H\"older observables for the measures of maximal entropy. The class of maps that are SEE includes all C^{\infty}-interval maps with h_{top}(f )>0 and all Viana maps.

papers.title: Almost Every Pair of Interval Exchange Transformations Does Not Generate a Free Group
papers.abstract: We show that the Lebesgue measure of the set of pairs of interval exchange transformations that generate a free group of rank $2$ is zero.

papers.title: The Dynamics of RMSProp Beyond the Stability Threshold
papers.abstract: We study what happens to RMSProp when the learning rate is too large for convergence to the minimizer. For positive-definite quadratic loss functions, we show that the minimizer is Lyapunov un- stable above an explicit critical learning rate. Nevertheless, every trajectory eventually enters a compact trapping region. We obtain explicit bounds proportional to h in the spatial variables and to h2 in the memory variables, where h is the learning rate. We also prove that nontrivial period-two orbits exist precisely above the critical learning rate, and under additional spectral assumptions, an attracting branch of these orbits emerges from the minimizer. For sufficiently large learning rates, we construct branches near admissible corners of a cube. We then explore the dynamics inside the trapping region using the parameterization method and numerical continuation, exploring invariant circles and tori, coexistence of attracting sets, circle-doubling sequences, and chaotic motions. We examine how the dynamics depend on the loss Hessian, memory decay, and dimension. Finally, we test a learning-rate reduction schedule and continue selected invariant circles into an autonomous variant of the Adam optimizer.

papers.title: Approximability of deep computations
papers.abstract: This is the first of a series of papers in which we study deep computations (ultracomputations) and deep iterates, formalizing the ideas of "asymptotic limit" of computations and compositional iterates, respectively. In this first paper of the series, we characterize deep computations that are bona fide computable, and prove the existence of deep equilibria, which hitherto have been found only empirically in deep learning. A subsequent paper will study the complexity of ultracomputations. Our approach adapts and combines technology from topology of function spaces, structural Ramsey theory, topological dynamics, and model theory.

papers.title: Model-based computational study of reactive fluid systems using transfer operator methods
papers.abstract: In many industrial applications one aims for the design of efficient chemical reactions. This is often done using experimental analysis of the reactors in combination with numerical twins. However, the simultaneous modeling of flow, mixing and chemical reaction remains a complicated task because the computational costs are still significant and oftentimes prohibitive. Here, we model and analyze mixing processes of chemical substances by a transfer operator method using the Lagrangian trajectories of passive particles. In practice, we represent the spatial distributions of the chemical species concentrations by density vectors. These are evolved by means of a stochastic transition matrix, which is obtained as a numerical approximation of a transfer operator. In a further step, we model the reaction of the fluids by specific update rules of the density vectors. The method is applicable for closed and open example systems and different chemical processes such as competitive consecutive reactions. We demonstrate that the dynamic processes are reflected well by this method. Furthermore, we evaluate the interdependence of the reaction fronts with Lagrangian coherent structures which we define using set-oriented methods that also work well on three dimensional data.

papers.title: On a conjecture of Velani
papers.abstract: We investigate the approximation of elements of the middle-third Cantor set by dyadic rationals, and natural extensions. We prove a conjecture of Velani, completing the metric theory for the Cantor measure. Our key method enables a quantitative study of the incommensurability of binary and ternary expansions of integers, initiated by Furstenberg. The method has other applications, e.g. $\sum_{k} |\hat{\mu}(2^k)|^\sigma < \infty$ for any $\sigma > 0$, where $\mu$ is the Cantor measure.

papers.title: The first $\ell^2$-Betti number, cost and rank gradient of few-relator random groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a random group in the few-relator model with $n\ge 2$ generators and $m\ge 1$ relators. We prove that asymptotically almost surely the first $\ell^2$-Betti number, the cost minus one, and the absolute rank gradient of $G$ are all equal to $\max\{n-m-1,0\}$. In particular, the equality $\beta_1^{(2)}(G)=0$ when $m\ge n-1$ answers positively a conjecture of Kielak, Kropholler and Wilkes [J. Lond. Math. Soc., 2022].

papers.title: Multiplicity of brake Reeb orbits on real prequantization bundles
papers.abstract: We prove multiplicity results for geometrically distinct brake Reeb orbits on real prequantization $S^1$-bundles under geometric and dynamical assumptions. The lower bounds are expressed in terms of the sum of the mod-two Betti numbers of the real locus of the base. Our proofs combine Lagrangian Rabinowitz Floer homology with the index iteration theory for brake orbits. As an application, we obtain a sharp lower bound for the number of brake geodesics on Finsler spheres with pinched flag curvature.

papers.title: Global shadow estimates and Hausdorff measure criteria in higher rank
papers.abstract: Patterson--Sullivan measures encode the distribution of orbits of discrete group actions near the boundary. We prove a global shadow lemma for Patterson--Sullivan measures associated to relatively Morse subgroups of higher-rank semisimple Lie groups. The estimate is uniform for shadows centered at arbitrary points in a Gromov model, including points deep in the cuspidal part, and expresses the contribution of each cusp in terms of peripheral growth. This extends the global shadow lemma of Stratmann--Velani for geometrically finite real hyperbolic groups. As applications, we establish local doubling and reverse doubling. Under Zariski density, we give necessary and sufficient criteria for Patterson--Sullivan measures to agree with the associated Hausdorff measures and to be Ahlfors regular. For symmetric linear forms, these criteria hold without Zariski density. We verify the criteria explicitly for cusped Hitchin representations and real-hyperbolic self-joinings.

papers.title: Regularity of Manhattan manifolds and exact dimensionality for relatively Anosov groups
papers.abstract: We establish several results about Patterson--Sullivan measures for relatively Anosov groups. First, we prove that these measures are exact dimensional with respect to visual metrics induced by Gromov models in the Groves--Manning quasi-isometry class. Under the additional assumption that the group is relatively Morse, we show that the associated scalar Cartan metric is Gromov hyperbolic and that the corresponding boundary premetric is a visual metric to which the exact-dimensionality theorem applies. Second, we prove that their Manhattan manifolds are $C^1$-regular, from which we deduce that the growth indicator is $C^1$-regular and strictly concave on the interior of the limit cone. This extends the case of Anosov representations by Kim--Oh--Wang. Our methods are dynamical, and we exploit the fact due to Kim--Oh and Blayac--Canary--Zhu--Zimmer that Bowen--Margulis--Sullivan measures for relatively Anosov groups are finite and mixing.

papers.title: TNODEV: Toolbox for Neural ODE Verification
papers.abstract: Neural ordinary differential equations (neural ODE) gained attention in safety critical settings such as continuous-time controllers for cyber-physical systems and classifiers integrated into automated decision pipelines, raising the question whether their behavior can be formally verified. Existing tools dedicated to neural ODE provide only a single reachability call without iterative input-set refinement, limiting the precision of their verdicts to whatever one reachability call can deliver. We present TNODEV, the first formal verifier for neural ODE that integrates a falsification checker, a fast interval-based reachability backend based on continuous-time mixed monotonicity, a verification and refinement loop with three input-set splitting heuristics, and a parallel scheduler in a single end-to-end pipeline. TNODEV supports safe-set inclusion verification on pure neural ODE, neural ODE in closed loop with a neural network controller and general neural ODE (GNODE), with the safe set specified either as an interval or as the half-space intersection induced by a target classification label. We evaluate TNODEV on a range of benchmarks across safe-set inclusion and classification-robustness properties, including a direct reachability comparison against NNV 2.0 and CORA and a verification comparison against NNV 2.0 on MNIST general neural ODE classifiers.

papers.title: Average measure theoretic entropy for a family of expanding on average random Blaschke products
papers.abstract: This work gives a computable formula for the average measure theoretic entropy of a family of expanding on average random Blaschke products, generalizing work by Pujals, Roberts and Shub [Expanding maps of the circle revisited: positive Lyapunov exponents in a rich family. $\textit{Ergodic Theory Dynam. Systems.}$ $\textbf{26}(6)$ $(2006),$ $1931$-$1937$] to the random setting. In doing so, we describe the random invariant measure and associated measure theoretic entropy for a class of admissible random Blaschke products, allowing for maps which are not necessarily expanding and may even have an attracting fixed point.
